problem_or_opportunity: The original HYPE-native breakout live seed was strongest before unsupported cross-asset transfer, while the later HYPE-native losses were concentrated in a different completed 15-minute context. Determine whether long entries initiated during explicit TREND_DOWN context explain a material part of that deterioration without changing the native signal or exit contract.
why_now: The exact 14-trade HYPE lineage shows every original entry occurred in TREND_UP or RANGE, while six of seven later entries occurred in TREND_DOWN. This association is post-observation and profile/time confounded, so it requires one frozen mechanistic comparison before it can influence any proposal.

predeclared_experiment.control: long entry authority on every native long onset; native short onset remains exit-only
predeclared_experiment.challenger: identical control except native long entries with completed context_15m=TREND_DOWN are censored
predeclared_experiment.unchanged_signals: native short onsets remain present and may close an open long

success_metrics: development net return, profit factor, maximum drawdown, trade count, and net excluding largest winner
chronological development fold results for control and challenger
already-opened final 60-day descriptive results with no selection authority
exact count of censored long signals and preservation of short exit signals
separate long-side economics under identical fees, slippage, funding, stop, and fixed hold
risks_and_failure_modes: The hypothesis was selected after inspecting 14 live lifecycles, so apparent improvement can be selection bias.
Time, profile generation, direction, and regime are confounded in the small live sample.
Censoring entries changes lifecycle occupancy and therefore later signal availability.
One-minute bars cannot reproduce private IOC queue state or intrabar mark/stop ordering.
A positive already-opened block cannot be treated as untouched validation.
A regime filter may reduce cadence without establishing absolute positive expectancy.
validation_plan: Write tests before implementation proving only TREND_DOWN long entries are censored.
Prove native short signals remain in the stream and retain opposite-onset exit authority.
Run one immutable comparison with no threshold or parameter search.
Verify output identity, report-only authority, largest-winner sensitivity, and chronological folds.
Do not change v53, v54 observer authority, sizing, leverage, routes, or exits from this experiment.

decision_rules.reject: Challenger does not materially improve development winner-robust economics or makes absolute economics worse.
decision_rules.defer: Challenger improves development but remains negative, fold-unstable, or dependent on the largest winner.
decision_rules.prospective_observer_only: Challenger is positive and winner-robust in development and consistent in the already-opened descriptive block; this still grants no live authority and must be frozen prospectively.

falsifiers: A challenger output censors a non-TREND_DOWN long signal or removes a short exit signal.
Results change without changing the frozen market evidence or declared contract.
Development improvement disappears after removing the largest winner or is isolated to one fold.
A compatible prospective sample shows the censored context is profitable after exact costs.
Any live runtime, strategy, route, risk, leverage, or configuration changes during this report-only test.

explicit_approval.scope: No live strategy, route, asset, parameter, leverage, sizing, risk, or execution authority is granted.
